title: MetricPrompt: Prompting Model as a Relevance Metric for Few-shot Text Classification

problem.claim: Few-shot text classification performance with prompting models depends substantially on prompt-template and verbalizer design.

gap.claim: Verbalizer design remains difficult, and the gap between pre-trained language-model pre-training objectives and text classification limits smooth adaptation.

contributions.claim: MetricPrompt reformulates few-shot text classification as text-pair relevance estimation to reduce verbalizer design difficulty.
MetricPrompt uses a prompting model as the relevance metric and jointly takes a training sample and a query sample to capture cross-sample relevance information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evaluation spans three widely used text-classification datasets and four few-shot settings.
The authors report that MetricPrompt outperforms manual and other automatic verbalizer-design methods across all evaluated few-shot settings and achieves new state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prompting methods perform strongly across text-mining tasks, particularly few-shot tasks.
Prompting-model performance depends heavily on prompt-template and verbalizer design.
MetricPrompt reformulates few-shot classification as text-pair relevance estimation and uses prompting models to estimate relevance.
The method jointly uses training and query samples to capture cross-sample relevance information.
Experiments cover three datasets and four few-shot settings, with reported improvements over baseline verbalizer approaches.

source_observation.claim: The method reframes classification as relevance estimation and jointly considers a training sample with a query sample.

interpretation.claim: Recasting a task around a relation that aligns more closely with the model's pre-training objective may reduce task-specific output-design burden and expose useful cross-example information.

application.claim: For few-shot classification with difficult label verbalizers, consider formulations based on pairwise relevance between examples and queries.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the evaluated text-classification datasets and few-shot settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not describe the prompt templates, verbalizer construction details, or training procedure.
The abstract does not provide ablations or independent verification of the reported results.
